Service Satisfaction and Churn Rate by Tenure

Average Service Satisfaction (left) · Churn Rate (right) vs Tenure (months)
Average Service SatisfactionChurn Rate
Across all customers (active and churned), churn rate is highest for the newest customers and falls steadily as tenure grows, while satisfaction rises. The Target Boundary marks that crossover — it's why the target list can include very-low-tenure customers: that's precisely where churn risk concentrates. (The Retention Boundary is applied separately, to each customer's SVR-predicted tenure — it isn't a second point on this chart's tenure axis.)
This chart is a descriptive summary — average Service Satisfaction and Churn Rate grouped by tenure across all customers — used here to justify the boundary choice. The SVM and SVR models operate independently of it: each predicts from an individual customer's full profile rather than from this aggregate trend.
